
\subsection{Exact 1024-bit Sparse-Center Certificate}
\label{app:exact-1024-certificate}

The following certificate replaces the earlier 1024-bit-scale demonstrator with an exact
1024-bit semiprime.  Let $r=512$ and let the sparse center offset be supported on
bit positions
\[
\{2,30,38,66\}.
\]
Thus
\[
z = 73786976570789855236,
\qquad
A = 2^{512}+z,
\qquad
|\mathcal Z|=\binom{128}{4}=10668000,
\qquad
\kappa(\mathcal Z)=23.346786.
\]

The generated primes are
\begin{align*}
p &= 5641338196453751900558169133899445965512943171921653249005071240764140502880990440301298805937126654471794360563825782236514628485101723326542540443641577,\\
q &= 21174277663431442298589880862512246289445788469263133506442051646679387557266103513302449790396680200908269355809146319470993137138791564140277899148237087.
\end{align*}
Their product is the exact 1024-bit semiprime
\[
n = .
\]
The half-difference is
\[
B = 7766469733488845199015855864306400161966422648670740128718490202957623527192556536500575492229776773218237497622660268617239254326844920406867679352297755.
\]
The verification identities are
\[
\frac{p+q}{2}=A,
\qquad
A-2^{512}=z,
\qquad
A^2-n=B^2,
\qquad
n=pq.
\]
Moreover, $p$ and $q$ are prime, $\operatorname{bitlength}(p)=511$,
$\operatorname{bitlength}(q)=513$, and $\operatorname{bitlength}(n)=1024$.
The classical Fermat iteration count from $\lceil\sqrt n\rceil$ to the true center
is
\[
I_{\rm Fermat}=A-\lceil\sqrt n\rceil = 2478431856029077648146734920559655278592319681355949986143986025196410605708673301325582864092398286350571183537840547006975914182782595548458181903614248,
\]
which has bit length 510.  In contrast, the sparse shifted-shell search is confined
to $\binom{128}{4}$ candidate offsets before QR sieving and exact square certification.
